insights.insight: Crinkl is processing roughly $13,700–$14,000 in cryptographically verified GMV per day across confirmed receipts, with cumulative volume past $4.6M and tracking toward $5M — a deterministic purchase signal at a scale that makes probabilistic cookie-based inference look structurally weak by comparison.

In the trailing 14-day window, grocery-supermarkets (1,397 receipts / $62K) and retail-department-stores (818 receipts / $34K) account for the majority of verified receipt volume — the categories where brand marketers spend the most on shopper targeting are where purchase proof is densest.

insights.topic: Walmart leads verified brand receipt density
insights.insight: Walmart holds 323 receipts in the 14-day trailing window, nearly double second-place Kroger (147) and Costco (143) — for CPG and mass-market brands, Walmart shopper verification is the highest-density signal currently available in this dataset.

Restaurants-and-dining crossed the visibility threshold in the trailing aggregate window as of Oct 30, contributing 1,031 receipts and $32K in verified spend — QSR and casual-dining brands now have a confirmed category signal to evaluate for post-purchase targeting use cases.

Two new brands crossed the receipt-density visibility threshold within 96 hours after a 40-snapshot freeze — 7-Eleven signals convenience-channel penetration and UPS Store signals service-retail, both categories historically underserved by purchase-verified targeting data.

Active metro coverage has reached 19 confirmed CBSA cells, with CBSA 11700 appearing in two consecutive snapshots — geographic reach is widening incrementally, but marketers should treat current footprint as regional rather than national scale until cell count grows materially.
